body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s a warm and quiet Sunday to start your day, but we’re waking up to some heavy news: an elderly woman rescued from an East Bakersfield house fire earlier this week has died, and we’re also tracking a busy night for first responders along the Kern River and local roadways. Expect a high near 91 degrees today with moderate air quality, so keep the windows open and the water close as you head into the afternoon.

## The Kern Overnight

The night was anything but still for Kern County’s first responders, with a dramatic water rescue, a foot chase, and a hit-and-run on the interstate keeping crews moving late into the evening. The most significant call came from the Kern River near the Kern River Golf Course, where a woman was reported to have gone into the water and floated for roughly an hour toward Lake Ming. The reporting party, who had been in the river with her, told dispatchers that both had gotten out and there was no reason she would have gone back in, but crews still launched a search of the bank behind the golf course. After a tense period of searching, responders reported they had located her at a camp just southeast of the golf course area, bringing the incident to a safe close.

Elsewhere, officers were involved in a foot chase along the canal bank near Rosedale Highway after a man with a satchel was tracked southbound and then eastbound toward the water. A caller reported seeing him discard items near a chain link fence in a clearing by a tree, and officers eventually recovered currency from the suspect. They asked for a victim to be brought by for an in-field identification, though no further details were immediately available. On the roads, CHP was hunting a Freightliner Cascadia that struck a Kenworth on northbound Interstate 5 just north of the county line and kept going. The victim vehicle was still on the shoulder less than half a mile north of the county line about two hours later, a reminder of how close calls can linger on the highway.

Fire crews also stayed busy with a shed fire on the 800 block of Exchange Street, where people at the property were trying to put it out before engines arrived, and a rubbish fire along the railroad tracks on Edison Highway. A man on 19th Street told dispatchers he had been knocked unconscious and was bleeding, prompting an ambulance request. The overnight log also included a welfare check on East Cedar Street at Franklin Field, where a man was reported in a 2008 Ford Escape with a rope, and a vehicle-versus-pedestrian incident at Lincoln Street and Pierce, where the pedestrian was up and walking and did not appear injured.

## Today's weather

It’s a classic late-summer day in Kern County, with the mercury climbing to a high near 91 degrees and dipping to a comfortable low around 66 degrees overnight. Right now, it’s a mild 66 degrees at Meadows Field, and there are no active weather alerts for the county. Air quality is sitting at a moderate 58 on the AQI scale, so sensitive groups might want to take it a little easier outdoors, but for most of us it’s a pleasant morning to get out and enjoy the sunshine before the heat builds.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Kern County has honored 127 residents for POW/MIA Remembrance Day**, a solemn and important recognition for those who served and never came home. The ceremony brought together veterans, families, and community members to remember the sacrifices of prisoners of war and those still missing in action, ensuring their stories are not forgotten. It’s a reminder of the deep military roots in this valley and the gratitude we owe to those who gave so much.

**According to 23ABC, the elderly woman rescued from a burning East Bakersfield home has died at Kern Medical.** The fire broke out in the 1300 block of Ralston Street on September 17, and firefighters found heavy smoke pouring from the home with neighbors shouting that someone was still inside. Locked gates and a locked front door slowed the rescue, but crews used a rotary saw and irons to force their way in, finding the woman unconscious and carrying her to safety. She regained consciousness and was taken to Kern Medical, but died on September 18; her identity has not been released.

**23ABC also reports that a Duarte man has been arrested for allegedly arranging to meet a 16-year-old minor for a lewd purpose** through the online chat platform Monkey. Romulus Chan Reynera faces charges related to the meeting, and local advocates are using the case to urge parents to talk openly with their children about online safety. Nearly 45% of kids between 7 and 18 report seeing inappropriate content online, and more than 6 in 10 interact with unknown users daily, so the message is clear: keep the conversation going.

**KGET 17 tells us that CSUB has added a mariachi course to its curriculum**, bringing the richness of the music to campus for students to learn and perform. The new offering celebrates a cherished Mexican musical tradition and gives students a chance to connect with cultural heritage in a hands-on way. It’s a wonderful addition to the university’s offerings and a sign of the valley’s vibrant diversity.

**Bakersfield Now reports that an elderly woman was rescued from an east Bakersfield house fire**, a story that has since taken a tragic turn with her passing. The initial rescue was a coordinated effort involving neighbors who alerted crews and firefighters who broke through locked barriers to reach her. While the outcome is heartbreaking, the quick actions of those on the scene are a testament to the community’s care for its own.

## Something good

On a lighter note, California State University, Bakersfield has launched a mariachi course, giving students the chance to learn and perform a beloved musical tradition right here on campus. It’s a joyful way to celebrate cultural richness and bring the community together through music. Whether you’re a student or just a fan of the genre, it’s a sweet reminder of the good things happening in our valley.

## Coming up this week

There’s plenty on the calendar this week to keep you busy. The Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets Monday, September 21 at noon, followed by the Homelessness committee on Tuesday, September 22 at noon, and the Laws and Legislation Committee on Friday, September 25 at noon—all open to the public. Over at the Fox Theater, the Cults & Classics series continues Monday, September 21 with *What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?*, and MEN I TRUST takes the stage Wednesday, September 23. MIKE SHERM follows on Saturday, September 26, so there’s no shortage of entertainment to round out your week.
